# A01-S38: Correspondence

Correspondence extract. [████] marks redaction; […] marks omission.

[…] 
I came across a Russian Netflix sci-fi series, Better than us, which is odd in one way or another, but world goals and HH topics keep 18appearing, which I have not seen before. In some way it is more “honest” in its approach to the future and at the same time, amidst all the sci-fi stuff, old junkers of gasoline-powered cars drive around – as if they thought “it is simply too expensive to produce driverless or flying cars – fuck it, we’ll go all out on everything else” 😁🙈

1. episode starts with a child reading the following rules aloud:
The first law: A robot may not harm a human being or, through passivity, allow a human to come to harm.
The second law: The robot must obey any order given by a human. Except in cases where the order conflicts with the first law.
The third law: The robot must protect its own existence as long as this does not conflict with the first or second law.

So the scene is set.

There are many small pearls, and they come every time I think, do I want to see more. For example, a Russian ministry is sitting and talking with a robot company (which controls the sale of advanced robots) about the future of work life. The business owner says something like: Why not give people a good pension? We have an average life expectancy of 70 and our retirement age is 65 (which is actually true, a law Putin got introduced/snuck in during the Winter Olympics in Russia). We can let people work until they are 45 years old, then they have trained the robots in the position and they can take over the job, it's cheaper to operate, people can get a better pension for a longer time.

They only speak Russian.

I have also seen a light comedy with among others Susan Sarandon, called Robot and Frank. It’s about a demented father who gets a helper robot from his son, very much against his will, but ends up being happy with it, because he can teach it things which was definitely not the original intention. (killing time in a cozy way)
